questions.q: Which algorithm requires the list to be sorted before it can be used?
questions.why: Binary search discards half the list each time, which only works if the list is in order.

questions.q: A bubble sort (ascending) is run on 4 2 7 1. What is the list after the first pass?
A binary search looks for 23 in the sorted list 4 11 15 19 23 30 42. Which item is checked first?
questions.why: Indices 0 to 6 give mid = 3, which holds 19.

questions.q: Describe how a merge sort works.
questions.model: The list is split in half repeatedly until each sub-list holds one item. Pairs of sub-lists are then merged, comparing their first items and taking the smaller each time, until one sorted list remains.
points: repeatedly divide list in half until single items
merge pairs by comparing first items and taking the smaller
